description: This pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the distribution of media outlets categorized by their framing narrative, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet or group. The chart is divided into 15 distinct segments, each labeled with the name of a media entity and a numerical value indicating its proportional share. The largest segment, labeled “Breitbart,” occupies 14% of the chart and is colored blue. The second largest segment, “Drudge Report,” accounts for 8% and is orange. Another 8% is allocated to “The Daily Caller,” shown in green. “Other” constitutes 13% and is gray. Several outlets share smaller proportions: “Fox News,” “CNN,” “PoliticusUSA,” and “Shareblue” each represent 3%, while “RT,” “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Red State,” and “Daily Mail” each represent 3%. “BBC” and “The Guardian” each account for 4%, “Vox” and “NPR” each represent 6%, and “The Huffington Post” represents 5%. The chart includes a legend that maps the names to their respective colors, and each slice displays its corresponding numerical value. The segments are arranged in descending order of size around the chart’s circumference, starting from the largest at the top right and proceeding clockwise.
